newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico sees higher 1996 oilseed production.
newsitem.headline: Mexico sees higher 1996 oilseed production.

text.p: Mexico will produce 550,000 tonnes of oilseeds in 1996, up from 515,000 tonnes in 1995, a forecasts by a private business group said.

The Eastern Cooking Oils chamber said in a report obtained by Reuters that Mexico will produce 40,000 tonnes of sesame seed; 350,000 tonnes of cottonseed, 150,000 tonnes of rapeseed and 10,000 tonnes of soybeans.
Soybean production is expected to drop to its lowest level in the past decade, down from 135,000 tonnes in 1995 and the record 709,000 tonnes in 1980.
Oilseed production will be insufficent for the industry, requiring continued imports, the report said.
"Agricultural production from Mexican farms, the nation's primary source of oilseeds, meets about 17.91 percent of its requirements, while the rest must come from outside Mexico," the report said.
"In oils and fats, production will reach only 19.16 percent, and at least 80 percent will need to be imported," the chamber said.

In 1995, Mexico's vegetable oil industries used 3.56 million tonnes of oilseed, of which 2.92 million tonnes were imported. In addition, 2.23 million tonnes of soybeans and 558,101 tonnes of canola were exported.
